author: Mark Atwood
text:
Cascade from PKIX-fmtv.17's rescope decision (Mark, 2026-05-12, attended):

This bead's deliverable is now well-defined. Blocks on:
- **PKIX-fmtv.22** — TLS hostname corpus (the only corpus pyca's `PolicyBuilder` can consume)

**Scope is intrinsically TLS-only on pyca's side:**
- pyca has `PolicyBuilder().build_server_verifier(DNSName(...))` — used for verify_tls_server differential
- pyca has `PolicyBuilder().build_client_verifier(...)` — used for verify_tls_client_dns differential (once PKIX-fmtv.11.2 client half ships)
- pyca has **no** S/MIME verifier — verify_smime_signer / verify_smime_recipient have no pyca oracle. Differential testing for S/MIME falls entirely to PKIX-fmtv.18 (OpenSSL).
- pyca has **no** code-signing verifier — same.
- pyca has **no** timestamp verifier — same.
- pyca has **no** OCSP responder verifier — same.

This scope gap is **not a defect** — it reflects pyca's intentional API surface (PolicyBuilder is TLS-focused). Documenting it explicitly in the deliverable so future contributors don't try to fill it.

Acceptance: per-purpose pass-rate documented in pkix-difftest/baseline-verify-pyca.md. Two purposes (TLS server, TLS client) covered; all other wrappers explicitly noted as "no pyca oracle available, see baseline-verify-openssl.md".

Releasing stale claim, removing human label.
